o.text: Inherited from Proto-Turkic *ẹk(k)i (“two”). Cognate with Turkish iki.
From Classical Azerbaijani دِگُلْ (degül), from Old Anatolian Turkish دِكُلْ (degül), from Proto-Turkic *tegül (“is not”). Cognate with Turkish değil, Turkmen däl.

Borrowed from Persian زور (zor).
The adjective's sense of excellent or amazing is an ameliorative semantic shift from the original sense of terrifying. Compare Uzbek zo‘r where a similar shift happened. Also compare English terrific.
From Persian علاقهدار. By surface analysis, əlaqə + -dar.
Borrowed from Arabic غَيْر (ḡayr). Cognate with Turkish gayr (Ottoman Turkish غیر (gayr)), Turkmen gaýr, Uyghur غەير (gheyr), Uzbek gʻayr.
